To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency spike — Hosted API p99 after scale-up

Hi Michael,

We saw a sharp spike in p99 and p95 tail latency starting ~07:55 PDT when our traffic hit a new peak and Redwood's hosted endpoint autoscaled. The first requests that hit new GPU instances had "first byte" delays around 3–6s; subsequent requests were fine. This is causing checkout timeouts for some users.

Quick details:
- Endpoint: POST /v1/generate (model: rw-13b-quant)
- Time window: 07:55–08:05 PDT
- Symptoms: high initial TTFB after autoscaler spin; errors were rare, mostly timeouts at client side

We've attached a short capture and sample traces. Can you confirm whether this matches a known cold model-loading behavior and how quickly Redwood can mitigate?

Thanks,
Rajiv
Ops / Acme Payments

Folks — initial triage below.

What I see in the traces Rajiv attached:
- For scale-up events that create a new GPU instance, the first request to that instance shows TTFB spikes of ~3–6s.
- Median request latency on the triggered pool once populated is normal (~120–180ms).
- p95 across the window was ~1.3s; p99 hit ~4.6s.
- No apparent model execution errors; CPU and network during the window show short bursts that align with model weights transfer and CUDA kernel JIT paths.

Attachments: p99_trace_0503.json (trace with per-request timing).

Immediate ask: Priya, can SRE check whether model weight staging and kernel JIT are happening on the hot path and whether we can pre-stage weights for large models?

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Production latency spike — Hosted API p99 after scale-up

Thanks for the data. Root-cause summary after quick investigation:

- Cause: When the hosted autoscaler creates new GPU workers for a burst, model binaries and tokenizer artifacts are loaded from object storage and a small set of CUDA kernels go through on-node JIT/initialization. For large models (rw-13b and similar), that path adds 2–5s to the first request.
- Why p99: Only a fraction of requests land on a freshly-provisioned instance during the window; those are the samples that dominate p99.

Short-term mitigations (can ship within hours):
1) Route the customer to a warm pool (we can pin a small reserved pool for Acme while we roll out a fix).
2) Add a fast fallback path that returns a slightly lower-context answer from a warm, quantized CPU instance for the first request (configurable per-account).
3) Tune autoscaler to prefer warm spare capacity at the cost of a small uplift in reserved units during business hours.

Medium-term (days):
- Implement asynchronous model prefetch on scale-up so first incoming request waits for prefetch + quick lightweight health probe rather than triggering full model init on the hot path.
- Cache precompiled CUDA kernels in the instance image to avoid JIT at request time.

I've opened a Jira ticket with proposed work: INF-9823. Attaching CPU/GPU utilization snapshot from the window.

Priya Natarajan
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: cpu_gpu_util_0503.csv (text/csv)]

Good investigation — thanks, Priya. Action items I propose: 

1) Immediate (hours): provision a small warm GPU pool for Acme (manual routing) and enable the CPU fallback for the first request. Engineering will own running that route and communicating cutover to Acme.
2) Short (48–72 hours): ship an asynchronous prefetch + probe path; should reduce observed TTFB for the first real request to <500ms in the common case. INF-9823 will track this.
3) Medium (2 weeks): bake kernel caches into images and optimize model artifact layout.

For customer communication, I'd like a short executive note and a credit offer. Michael / Aditya — can you propose language? Priya, please mark the Jira ticket with a high priority.

Evelyn Hart

Rajiv — on behalf of Redwood, I'm sorry for the disruption this morning. We take tail latency incidents seriously. TL;DR: we identified that new GPU workers can add model-load and kernel init overhead to the first request after scale-up which impacted your p99.

What we're doing:
- Short-term: routing you to a small warm GPU pool now and enabling a CPU fallback for first requests (already in progress).
- Work in flight: INF-9823 to implement asynchronous prefetch + probe; target rollout within 72 hours.
- We will follow up with a post-incident report once INF-9823 is shipped.

As a gesture of goodwill we're offering a one-time credit of $10,000 against May invoice and a dedicated check-in next week to validate regressions do not recur. Please sign the attached exec summary to acknowledge the plan and credit.

Apologies again — Michael will coordinate the follow-up.

Best,
